Jeshaiah
jeh-SHY-uh
proper noun
Hebrew Yeshayah (H3470), the LORD has saved — from yasha (H3467), to save, to deliver, and Yah; the same Hebrew name the Authorized Version renders Isaiah for the prophet, and Jeshaiah or Jesaiah for these other men.

Biblical Definition

Several men bear this name, none of them the prophet. One is a son of Hananiah in the royal line of David after the captivity, spelled Jesaiah (1Ch 3:21). One is a son of Jeduthun, among the singers who prophesied with a harp, to give thanks and to praise the LORD, and leader of the eighth of the twenty-four courses (1Ch 25:3, 15). One is a Levite of the sons of Eliezer, in the line set over the treasures of the house of God (1Ch 26:25). One came up from Babylon with Ezra at the head of seventy males of the sons of Elam (Ezr 8:7), and another with the sons of Merari (Ezr 8:19). One more stands in a Benjamite pedigree of those who dwelt at Jerusalem (Neh 11:7). The name says the LORD has saved, in the perfect tense: not that He will, or may, but that He has. It is the same confession that the prophet Isaiah carried through sixty-six chapters and that reappears in Greek as the name given to Mary's son, for he shall save his people from their sins (Mat 1:21).

Origin & Era

The name of several men — a descendant of David, a son of Jeduthun among the singers, a Levite, and two who returned with Ezra. It means the LORD has saved.

JESHAIAH, Hebrew Yeshayah, the LORD has saved; the same name as Isaiah.

1. A son of Hananiah in the royal line of Judah after the captivity; written Jesaiah.

2. A son of Jeduthun, and leader of the eighth course of the singers.

3. A Levite of the sons of Eliezer, over the treasures of the house of God.

4. One who came up with Ezra at the head of seventy males of the sons of Elam.

Key Scripture

1Ch 25:3 — "Of Jeduthun: the sons of Jeduthun; Gedaliah, and Zeri, and Jeshaiah, Hashabiah, and Mattithiah, six, under the hands of their father Jeduthun, who prophesied with a harp, to give thanks and to praise the LORD."

1Ch 26:25 — "And his brethren by Eliezer; Rehabiah his son, and Jeshaiah his son, and Joram his son, and Zichri his son, and Shelomith his son."

Ezr 8:7 — "And of the sons of Elam; Jeshaiah the son of Athaliah, and with him seventy males."

Neh 11:7 — "And these are the sons of Benjamin; Sallu the son of Meshullam, the son of Joed, the son of Pedaiah, the son of Kolaiah, the son of Maaseiah, the son of Ithiel, the son of Jesaiah."

Modern Corruption

Salvation is spoken of as a process still to be completed; the name puts the decisive act in the perfect tense, already done.

expand to see more

Much popular religion keeps salvation permanently future and conditional — something a man hopes to obtain if he finishes well, so that assurance is presumption and the believer is meant to live in suspense. Scripture speaks in three tenses and refuses to collapse them. There is a past: by grace are ye saved through faith… it is the gift of God (Eph 2:8), and who hath saved us, and called us with an holy calling (2Ti 1:9). There is a present: unto us which are saved it is the power of God (1Co 1:18). And there is a future: now is our salvation nearer than when we believed (Rom 13:11).

The name Jeshaiah sits on the first of these, and it is the tense that grounds the others. Justification is a completed act of God, declaring the believer righteous once for all on the ground of Christ's imputed righteousness; sanctification is the lifelong work that follows; glorification is the certain end. To confuse the first with the second is to make a man's standing depend on his progress, which is the error the Reformation was fought over. The principle to recover is the order: because the LORD has saved, the believer may labour at holiness out of security rather than for it, and he which hath begun a good work in you will perform it until the day of Jesus Christ (Php 1:6).

Greek & Hebrew Roots

Hebrew Yeshayah (H3470), from yasha (H3467), to save, with Yah, the covenant name.

expand to see more

Hebrew yasha (H3467) — to save, deliver, give victory; the root of Joshua, Isaiah and Jesus.

Hebrew Yeshayah (H3470) — borne by several men; 1 Chronicles 3:21, 25:3, 26:25, Ezra 8:7, 8:19, Nehemiah 11:7.

Hebrew yeshuah (H3444) — salvation; the LORD is my light and my salvation (Psa 27:1).

Hebrew Yeshayahu — the longer form of the same name, rendered Isaiah for the prophet.

Greek sozo (G4982) — to save, to make whole; he shall save his people from their sins (Mat 1:21).

Usage

"“Gedaliah, and Zeri, and Jeshaiah, Hashabiah, and Mattithiah, six”."

"“Jeshaiah the son of Athaliah, and with him seventy males”."

"“The LORD has saved” — the confession in the perfect tense."
